items.stem: State any three points of significance of principles of management.
items.answer: Providing managers with useful insights into reality; Optimum utilisation of resources and effective administration; Scientific decisions; Meeting changing environment requirements; Fulfilling social responsibility; Management training, education and research
items.markingKey: Any three of: Providing managers with useful insights into reality; Optimum utilisation of resources and effective administration; Scientific decisions; Meeting changing environment requirements; Fulfilling social responsibility; Management training, education and research (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the points of significance of principles of management?
items.answer: Mainly behavioural
items.markingKey: (c) "Mainly behavioural" is one of the points describing the nature of principles of management, not one of the points of significance of principles of management.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about principles of management is NOT correct?
items.answer: They provide readymade solutions to every problem.
items.markingKey: (b) Incorrect statement: They provide readymade solutions to every problem.
options: They are general guidelines for managers.
They provide readymade solutions to every problem.
They are developed through practice and experimentation.

items.stem: The principles guide Siddharth at Reddy Brothers but do not give a ready solution to every problem. Which nature of management principles is highlighted?
items.answer: General guidelines
items.markingKey: (d) General guidelines. They are guidelines, not rigid rules.

items.stem: Aarav applies a principle differently when Sethi Traders faces a crisis than in normal times. Which nature of management principles is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Contingent. Application depends on the situation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Contingent; 2 marks for the justification: Application depends on the situation.

items.stem:
Nandini, a new manager at Kulkarni Agencies in Pune, says that management principles are useless because they do not tell her exactly what to do in each situation.
(i) Do you agree? Explain the nature of principles. (ii) State two benefits she will get by following them.
items.answer: (i) No: principles are general guidelines, flexible and contingent; they guide judgement rather than give ready solutions. (ii) Useful insights into reality, scientific decisions, optimum use of resources (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) No: principles are general guidelines, flexible and contingent; they guide judgement rather than give ready solutions. (ii) Useful insights into reality, scientific decisions, optimum use of resources (any two).

items.stem: Which concept is described here? "Management principles can be modified by the manager to suit the situation."
items.answer: Flexibility of principles
items.markingKey: (d) Flexibility of principles: Management principles can be modified by the manager to suit the situation.

items.stem: The same principle of division of work is used by Pillai Stores, a hospital and a school in Dehradun. Which nature of management principles is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Universal applicability. Principles apply to all organisations.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Universal applicability; 2 marks for the justification: Principles apply to all organisations.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Principles of management help in management training and research.
Reason (R): They are the basis of management as a discipline.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Gang plank"?
items.answer: A direct link between two employees at the same level in different departments, allowed by Fayol for quick communication in an emergency.
items.markingKey: (b) Gang plank: A direct link between two employees at the same level in different departments, allowed by Fayol for quick communication in an emergency.
options: Fayol's principle that there should be a place for everything and everyone, and everything and everyone should be in its place.
A direct link between two employees at the same level in different departments, allowed by Fayol for quick communication in an emergency.
Fayol's principle that managers should be kind and just to workers, with no discrimination on the basis of sex, religion, language, caste or nationality.
Fayol's principle that management should promote team spirit, unity and harmony among employees.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of unity of command but not of unity of direction?
items.answer: Implication: affects an individual employee
items.markingKey: (a) unity of command: Implication: affects an individual employee. The other options describe unity of direction.
options: Meaning: one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Unity of direction means that each employee has one boss.
Reason (R): Unity of direction prevents overlapping of activities.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: that is unity of command. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Fatima, a manager at Menon Retail, gives promotions only to people of her own region. Which of Fayol's principles is violated or applied here?
items.answer: Equity
items.markingKey: (c) Equity. No discrimination; kindness and justice to all.

items.stem: Bose Brothers has two separate heads and plans for two units making the same leather bags for the same market. Which of Fayol's principles is violated or applied here? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Unity of direction. One head and one plan for activities with the same objective.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Unity of direction; 2 marks for the justification: One head and one plan for activities with the same objective.

items.stem: Which of Fayol's principles is violated or applied here? In each case give a reason. (i) At Reddy Retail, both the management and workers honour the agreed rules, and penalties are imposed judiciously. (ii) A supervisor at Reddy Retail is given responsibility for output but no authority to requisition materials.
items.answer: (i) Discipline: Obedience to rules and agreements, with fair penalties. (ii) Authority and responsibility: Authority and responsibility should be balanced.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Discipline (ii) Authority and responsibility

items.stem:
At Pillai Stores, Aarav receives orders from both the production head and the quality head, and the two orders often conflict. Meanwhile, two branches selling the same stationery in Mumbai have different plans and heads.
(i) Identify the two principles violated. (ii) State one consequence of each violation.
items.answer: (i) Unity of command (dual orders) and unity of direction (two plans for the same objective). (ii) Confusion and indiscipline among workers; overlapping and wastage of resources.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Unity of command (dual orders) and unity of direction (two plans for the same objective). (ii) Confusion and indiscipline among workers; overlapping and wastage of resources.

items.stem:
At Kapoor Retail, Aarav receives orders from both the production head and the quality head, and the two orders often conflict. Meanwhile, two branches selling the same organic food products in Guwahati have different plans and heads.
(i) Identify the two principles violated. (ii) State one consequence of each violation.
items.answer: (i) Unity of command (dual orders) and unity of direction (two plans for the same objective). (ii) Confusion and indiscipline among workers; overlapping and wastage of resources.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Unity of command (dual orders) and unity of direction (two plans for the same objective). (ii) Confusion and indiscipline among workers; overlapping and wastage of resources.

Fayol is called the father of general management.

items.stem: Distinguish between unity of command and unity of direction on the basis of aim, meaning and relation.
items.answer: (i) Aim: unity of command: prevents dual subordination; unity of direction: prevents overlapping of activities. (ii) Meaning: unity of command: an employee receives orders from one superior only; unity of direction: one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective. (iii) Relation: unity of command: concerned with the functioning of personnel; unity of direction: concerned with the functioning of departments.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Aim: unity of command: prevents dual subordination; unity of direction: prevents overlapping of activities. (ii) Meaning: unity of command: an employee receives orders from one superior only; unity of direction: one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective. (iii) Relation: unity of command: concerned with the functioning of personnel; unity of direction: concerned with the functioning of departments.

items.stem: Which principle of Fayol is described here? "Fayol's principle that a formal line of authority runs from the highest to the lowest ranks, with a gang plank allowed for quick communication."
items.answer: Scalar chain
items.markingKey: (b) Scalar chain: Fayol's principle that a formal line of authority runs from the highest to the lowest ranks, with a gang plank allowed for quick communication.

items.stem: State any three principles of scientific management.
items.answer: Science, not rule of thumb; Harmony, not discord; Cooperation, not individualism; Development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity
items.markingKey: Any three of: Science, not rule of thumb; Harmony, not discord; Cooperation, not individualism; Development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity (1 mark each).

Assertion (A): Mental revolution is the essence of scientific management.

items.answer: Cooperation, not individualism. Cooperation between management and workers.

items.stem: Which principle of scientific management is applied? In each case give a reason. (ii) Sethi and Sons selects workers scientifically and trains them to reach their highest efficiency.
items.answer: (i) Harmony, not discord: Mental revolution creates harmony. (ii) Development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity: Scientific selection and training.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Harmony, not discord (ii) Development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity

items.stem:
Gupta and Sons pays ₹60 per unit to workers who make at least 12 units of toys a day and ₹50 per unit to those who make fewer. Fatima made 12 units and Imran made 11 units.
(i) Name the technique and calculate their daily wages. (ii) How does a difference of one unit affect wages, and why?
items.answer: (i) Differential piece wage system; Fatima: 12 × ₹60 = ₹720; Imran: 11 × ₹50 = ₹550. (ii) ₹170 difference; it rewards efficient workers and motivates others to reach the standard.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Differential piece wage system; Fatima: 12 × ₹60 = ₹720; Imran: 11 × ₹50 = ₹550. (ii) ₹170 difference; it rewards efficient workers and motivates others to reach the standard.

items.stem:
At Bose Industries, the production manager Manish finds workers make sports goods in different ways, take rest whenever they like, and machines often break down. He wants to apply scientific management.
(i) Suggest three techniques he should use, with a reason for each. (ii) Which principle should guide the relationship between him and the workers?
items.answer: (i) Method study (one best way), fatigue study (planned rest), functional foremanship with a repair boss (machine upkeep); also time study for standards. (ii) Harmony, not discord (mental revolution) and cooperation, not individualism.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Method study (one best way), fatigue study (planned rest), functional foremanship with a repair boss (machine upkeep); also time study for standards. (ii) Harmony, not discord (mental revolution) and cooperation, not individualism.

items.stem:
Vihaan runs Rao and Sons. At the head office he follows unity of command and a clear scalar chain, while in the factory he uses time study and specialist foremen.

items.answer: (i) Head office: Fayol; factory: Taylor. (ii) Partly (functional foremanship breaks unity of command) but they complement each other: one for overall administration, one for shop-floor productivity.

items.markingKey: (d) Functional foremanship: Taylor's technique of having eight specialist foremen, four in the planning department and four in the production department, to supervise workers.

items.stem: Workers at Bose Agencies are encouraged to suggest new ways of packing toys, and good suggestions are rewarded. Which of Fayol's principles is violated or applied here? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Initiative. Workers should be encouraged to take initiative.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Initiative; 2 marks for the justification: Workers should be encouraged to take initiative.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of unity of command but not of unity of direction?
items.answer: Meaning: an employee receives orders from one superior only
items.markingKey: (a) unity of command: Meaning: an employee receives orders from one superior only. The other options describe unity of direction.
options: Meaning: an employee receives orders from one superior only
Meaning: one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective

items.stem:
Diya, a new manager at Bose Brothers in Indore, says that management principles are useless because they do not tell her exactly what to do in each situation.
(i) Do you agree? Explain the nature of principles. (ii) State two benefits she will get by following them.
items.answer: (i) No: principles are general guidelines, flexible and contingent; they guide judgement rather than give ready solutions. (ii) Useful insights into reality, scientific decisions, optimum use of resources (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) No: principles are general guidelines, flexible and contingent; they guide judgement rather than give ready solutions. (ii) Useful insights into reality, scientific decisions, optimum use of resources (any two).

items.stem: The principles guide Imran at Mishra Agencies but do not give a ready solution to every problem. Which nature of management principles is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: General guidelines. They are guidelines, not rigid rules.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying General guidelines; 2 marks for the justification: They are guidelines, not rigid rules.

items.stem: What is meant by "Division of work"?
items.answer: Fayol's principle that work is divided into small tasks, each done by a trained specialist, leading to efficient output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Fayol's principle that work is divided into small tasks, each done by a trained specialist, leading to efficient output.

items.stem: Explain the following specialists under the production in-charge in functional foremanship: (i) Speed boss (ii) Gang boss.
items.answer: (i) Speed boss: Ensures that work is done at the required speed. (ii) Gang boss: Keeps machines and tools ready for workers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Ensures that work is done at the required speed. (ii) Keeps machines and tools ready for workers.

items.stem: Instead of trial and error, Saxena Stores uses work studies to find the best way to make electronic goods. Which principle of scientific management is applied?
items.answer: Science, not rule of thumb
items.markingKey: (d) Science, not rule of thumb. Scientific enquiry replaces rule of thumb.
options: Development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity

items.stem: Explain the following principles of management given by Henri Fayol: (i) Esprit de corps (ii) Unity of command.
items.answer: (i) Esprit de corps: Team spirit and unity among employees. (ii) Unity of command: Each employee receives orders from only one superior.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Team spirit and unity among employees. (ii) Each employee receives orders from only one superior.

items.stem: Diya at Jain Retail applies principles that are meant for the overall administration of the company from the top. Whose contribution is being described?
items.answer: Henri Fayol
items.markingKey: (a) Henri Fayol. Fayol's principles take a top-level view.

items.stem:
Joshi Agencies pays ₹60 per unit to workers who make at least 12 units of tea a day and ₹50 per unit to those who make fewer. Aditya made 12 units and Riya made 11 units.
(i) Name the technique and calculate their daily wages. (ii) How does a difference of one unit affect wages, and why?
items.answer: (i) Differential piece wage system; Aditya: 12 × ₹60 = ₹720; Riya: 11 × ₹50 = ₹550. (ii) ₹170 difference; it rewards efficient workers and motivates others to reach the standard.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Differential piece wage system; Aditya: 12 × ₹60 = ₹720; Riya: 11 × ₹50 = ₹550. (ii) ₹170 difference; it rewards efficient workers and motivates others to reach the standard.

items.stem: Distinguish between unity of command and unity of direction on the basis of relation, aim, meaning and implication.
items.answer: (i) Relation: unity of command: concerned with the functioning of personnel; unity of direction: concerned with the functioning of departments. (ii) Aim: unity of command: prevents dual subordination; unity of direction: prevents overlapping of activities. (iii) Meaning: unity of command: an employee receives orders from one superior only; unity of direction: one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective. (iv) Implication: unity of command: affects an individual employee; unity of direction: affects the entire organisation.
